title: Twist cancellation for a regular immersion
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient datum $k,\ell,E,n,\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and the constructible exceptional functors of [sk-def-purity-conv, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $N,m\geq0$ and $c\geq0$ satisfy $N=m+c$, and let $\omega_X\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $\omega_Z\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$ be equipped with isomorphisms
$$\Pi_X:\omega_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(N)[2N],\qquad \Pi_Z:\omega_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_Z(m)[2m],\qquad b:\omega_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!\omega_X.$$
Use the specified co-projection isomorphisms [lem-pur-coprojection] for the invertible Tate shifts. The following specified composite is an isomorphism:
$$\Phi(i;b,\Pi_X,\Pi_Z):\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\Pi_Z^{-1}(-m)[-2m]}\omega_Z(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{b(-m)[-2m]}(Ri^!\omega_X)(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{(Ri^!\Pi_X)(-m)[-2m]}(Ri^!(\Lambda_X(N)[2N]))(-m)[-2m]\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!(\Lambda_X(c)[2c]).$$
Here the last arrow is inverse co-projection followed by twist additivity and $N-m=c$. Cancelling the Tate shift gives $Ri^!\Lambda_X\cong\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]$, and the displayed target is a degree-zero sheaf isomorphic to $\Lambda_Z$. The data $b,\Pi_X,\Pi_Z$ are specified inputs; no regularity hypothesis, frame class, or normalization of these inputs is asserted.
